id_and_class.summary: Hedda Hassel Mørch defends a Russell-inspired panpsychism in which rudimentary consciousness is the intrinsic nature of matter, down to basic particles. Her distinctive claim is that phenomenal qualities are identical to causal powers: experiences such as pain or color are what make matter behave as it does. She links the hard problem of consciousness to the hard problem of matter and looks to Integrated Information Theory for help with the combination problem.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as the Causal Powers of Matter

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness, in primitive form, is the intrinsic nature of physical entities, and phenomenal properties are the categorical bases of their causal powers.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Physics describes the structure of the world and consciousness fills in its intrinsic nature; in Mørch's image, consciousness is the hardware that the software described by physics runs on.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not applicable (rudimentary consciousness is fundamental and ubiquitous; complex experience arises by combination)
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Qualia are non-structural properties we know from the inside, and Mørch holds they are essentially powerful rather than inert: the redness of red or the discomfort of hunger grounds how a system acts.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Fundamental physical entities whose intrinsic nature is experiential, and phenomenal properties identical to causal powers.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Introspective acquaintance with what experiences are like in themselves, combined with philosophical analysis of what physics leaves unspecified.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Micro-level experiences forming the structure that physics describes, with complex experiences built by combining them.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal consciousness, mental causation, and the intrinsic nature of matter.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Phenomenal properties are essentially dispositional, so feeling and causal power are one property seen from two sides.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Everywhere in the physical world, including basic particles, in rudimentary form.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Consciousness has real causal efficacy because phenomenal qualities are the very things that make matter behave as it does, which rules out epiphenomenalism.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: Mørch explores Integrated Information Theory as a way to explain how micro-experiences combine into complex ones.
core_claims_and_evidence: Phenomenal properties are identical to certain causal powers in the physical world.
The hard problem of matter calls for non-structural properties, and consciousness is the one phenomenon known to have them.
The hard problems of consciousness and matter complement each other more deeply than quantum-consciousness pairings that merely combine two mysteries.
Integrated Information Theory may help panpsychism with the combination problem.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical argument, drawing on neuroscience through Integrated Information Theory.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Mørch anticipates the charge that linking the hard problem of consciousness to the hard problem of matter is the same fallacy critics see in quantum theories, combining two mysteries in the hope they cancel.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: The combination problem, how micro-experiences make up complex ones, remains open, and her treatment of IIT as a remedy is exploratory.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Giving phenomenal properties causal powers answers the usual worry that Russellian panpsychism makes consciousness causally idle.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Every physical system has experiential matter at the base, but whether an AI forms a unified conscious subject depends on the unsolved combination problem.

sources_and_references.title_with_names: Non-physicalist Theories of Consciousness, Hedda Hassel Mørch
